articles.article_title: Opinion: The Sam Altman drama knocked Microsoft’s stock around. So why is its deal with OpenAI largely a secret to Wall Street? - MarketWatch
articles.article_text: Since OpenAI debuted ChatGPT a year ago, Microsoft’s stock has added more than $900 billion in market capitalization, and those two events are widely viewed by market participants as being related. When OpenAI surprisingly dismissed chief executive Sam Altman in November, Microsoft MSFT shares dove late in a Friday trading session and into after-hours trading . Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella jumped to action in response. After failing to negotiate a return for Altman over the following weekend, Nadella publicly offered to hire Altman and hundreds of other upset OpenAI workers before markets opened on Monday morning, when trading resumed and Microsoft shares jumped to a fresh all-time high . Jeremy Owens is MarketWatch’s technology editor and San Francisco bureau chief. You can follow him on Twitter @jowens510. Copyright © 2026 MarketWatch, Inc. All rights reserved.
articles.article_summary: More than four years after the companies officially established a "partnership," Microsoft has disclosed next to nothing in its securities filings about its deal with OpenAI, and confirmed to MarketWatch that executives don't believe it to be "material information."
